source.text:
Bayesian A/B Testing Is Not Immune to Peeking. Alex Molas. alexmolas.com, October 30 2025. https://www.alexmolas.com/2025/10/30/bayesian-ab-test-peeking.html Tier 2. Topics: 3,5. Why: simulation showing about 80% false positive rate when peeking every 100 obs and stopping at P(A>B)>0.95; corrects a common Bayesian myth.

CUPED variance reduction docs. Optimizely and Datadog. https://support.optimizely.com/hc/en-us/articles/33424529987597 and https://docs.datadoghq.com/experiments/statistics/cuped/ Tier 1. Topics: 7. Why: vendor implementation detail, 30-50% sample reduction claim, default-on behaviour.

PXL: A Better Way to Prioritize Your A/B Tests. Peep Laja / CXL. https://cxl.com/blog/better-way-prioritize-ab-tests/ Tier 3 (named practitioner). Topics: 9. Why: the actual PXL binary/evidence-weighted scorecard, an antidote to subjective ICE.

Guide to Multi-Armed Bandit: When to Do Bandit Tests. CXL. https://cxl.com/blog/bandit-tests/ Tier 3. Topics: 8. Why: named conditions (short campaigns, headlines, promotions) with Stephen Pavlovich's ecommerce reasoning on regret.

Stopping A/B Tests: How Many Conversions Do I Need? CXL. https://cxl.com/blog/stopping-ab-tests-how-many-conversions-do-i-need/ Tier 3. Topics: 1,2,4,13. Why: debunks "magic conversion number" rules and shows why 100/variant is not a threshold.

Sample ratio mismatch. Wikipedia + Automated SRM Detection (Gupta, Kohavi et al., ACM 2022). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sample_ratio_mismatch and https://dl.acm.org/doi/fullHtml/10.1145/3530019.3534982 Tier 1/2. Topics: 6. Why: chi-square method, worked p-value example, ~6% Microsoft rate.

Cart & Checkout UX research. Baymard Institute. https://baymard.com/blog/collections/cart-and-checkout Tier 1/2. Topics: 4,9,12. Why: 70.22% global average cart abandonment from a meta-analysis of 50 studies (last updated September 22 2025; the rate has held 69-71% since 2014), 11.3 average checkout form fields, up to 35.26% achievable checkout uplift and about $260B recoverable orders across US/EU; evidence for big-swing checkout hypotheses.

A/B Testing on Shopify without Plus / Shopify Plus checkout extensibility. Varify.io and Convert.com. https://varify.io/en/shopify-ab-testing-without-plus/ and https://www.convert.com/blog/shopify-ab-testing/optimize-shopify-checkout/ Tier 1/3. Topics: 12. Why: what is testable per Shopify plan, and the August 2024 extensibility change that killed client-side checkout A/B testing.

A/B testing on Shopify Checkout page. Shopify Developer Community (Liam-Shopify). shopify.dev, Nov-Dec 2024. https://community.shopify.dev/t/a-b-testing-on-shopify-checkout-page/3246 Tier 1. Topics: 12. Why: official confirmation there is no built-in checkout-extensibility A/B rule to show/hide customisations per group.

Designing A/B Testing Experiments for Long-Term Growth / Lessons from Kohavi and Sonnet. GrowthBook. https://www.growthbook.io/blog/designing-a-b-testing-experiments-for-long-term-growth Tier 2 (reports Kohavi data). Topics: 3,6,14. Why: the company-by-company win-rate and false-positive-risk table (Microsoft 33%, Bing 15%, Booking/Google/Netflix 10%, Airbnb 8%) with citations.

Useful secondary sources (Tier 3)

A/B Testing Statistics 2026 (DRIP experiment database). dripagency.de. https://dripagency.de/blog/ab-testing-statistics Tier 3. Topics: 14. Why: named-sample ecommerce win rates (36.3% win, 41.6% inconclusive, +2.77% median RPV) from a real test database, with the caveat that research pre-qualification raises win rate.

A/B Test Win Rate: Real Benchmarks From 2,288 Audited Tests. ConversionTeam. https://www.conversionteam.com/ab-test-win-rate/ Tier 3. Topics: 14. Why: 19.1% significant win rate on a stated 2,288-test sample, cross-checked against platform benchmarks.

Most of your A/B tests will fail (and that's OK). Oliver Palmer. https://www.oliverpalmer.com/blog/most-ab-tests-fail/ Tier 3. Topics: 14. Why: cites the Thomke/Ghosh 20,000-experiment Optimizely meta-analysis (10% significant uplift).

Ratio, Revenue, and Conversion Metrics in Optimizely. Atticus Li. atticusli.com, March 2026. https://atticusli.com/blog/posts/optimizely-ratio-revenue-conversion-metrics-guide/ Tier 3. Topics: 11. Why: the concrete variance numbers (97% spend $0, CoV ~750%, revenue needs ~6x traffic, 28k vs 175k per variant) and the winsorization workaround.

Avoid these common mistakes when estimating revenue from A/B tests. Conversionista. https://conversionista.com/blogs/avoid-these-common-mistakes-when-estimating-revenue-from-ab-tests/ Tier 3. Topics: 11. Why: worked example where higher conversion rate yields lower revenue, and the outlier problem in revenue inference.

Variance Reduction in A/B Testing. GrowthBook. https://www.growthbook.io/blog/variance-reduction-ab-testing Tier 1. Topics: 7,11. Why: practical CUPED/winsorization/threshold-metric guidance with the $5,000-order example.

Frequentist vs Bayesian A/B Testing: A Practitioner's Guide. DRIP / dripagency.de. https://dripagency.de/blog/bayesian-vs-frequentist-ab-testing Tier 3. Topics: 5. Why: the flat-prior critique (commercial Bayesian tools collapse to frequentist) stated plainly.

The Complete Guide to A/B Testing Platforms: Statistical Engine Comparison. Atticus Li. medium.com. https://medium.com/@atticusli/the-complete-guide-to-a-b-testing-platforms-a-statistical-engine-comparison-guide-a3cc4124cdf5 Tier 3. Topics: 5,12. Why: maps each platform's engine (Optimizely mSPRT+FDR, VWO Beta-Binomial, Eppo shrinkage, Statsig sequential).

When to Use Multi-Armed Bandit vs A/B Testing. Monetate. https://monetate.com/resource/when-to-use-multi-armed-bandit-testing-vs-a-b-testing/ Tier 3. Topics: 8. Why: ecommerce-specific bandit use for promotions and short-term initiatives.

Multi-Armed Bandit Testing vs A/B Testing (by vertical). leadgen-economy.com. https://www.leadgen-economy.com/blog/multi-armed-bandit-vs-ab-testing-when-each-wins/ Tier 3. Topics: 8. Why: the hybrid ecommerce pattern and the two-week-to-power note for a $100M retailer.

The A/B Testing Process That Separates 8- and 9-Figure DTC Brands. SplitBase. https://splitbase.com/blog/ab-testing Tier 3. Topics: 4,10. Why: DTC-specific "test fewer, bigger things on higher-traffic pages" and the A/B/n same-question rule.

Most A/B Tests Cannot Detect a Real Win. aiformarketing.news. https://aiformarketing.news/insights/ab-testing-underpowered.html Tier 3. Topics: 4,6. Why: the under-100,000-visitors/month "bold changes only" gate and re-test-surprising-winners-with-a-holdout rule.

A/B Testing With Low Traffic. customerimpact.be. https://www.customerimpact.be/en/blog/ab-testing-low-traffic/ Tier 3. Topics: 4. Why: the honest conditions under which sequential before/after is defensible and when it is not.

A/B testing for pricing (2026). Kirro and gempages. https://kirro.io/ab-testing-pricing and https://gempages.net/blogs/shopify/a-b-testing-pricing Tier 3. Topics: 12. Why: the Amazon 2000 case (6,896 refunds, $3.10 avg), EU personalised-price disclosure rule, negative vs positive price discrimination, and "test framing not the number."

Convert.com Flicker Effect glossary + AB Tasty flicker guide + DebugBear anti-flicker analysis. https://www.convert.com/glossary/flicker-effect/ , https://www.abtasty.com/blog/ab-testing-flicker-effect/ , https://www.debugbear.com/blog/ab-testing-anti-flicker-body-hiding Tier 1/2. Topics: 6,12. Why: FOOC mechanism, "no miracle fix," and the 3-4s anti-flicker page-hide cost (DebugBear, Feb 2022, updated Dec 2025).

Client-Side vs Server-Side Experiments. AB Tasty / Wingify (Natalia Soto), May 2020, updated 2026. https://www.abtasty.com/blog/client-server-side-experiments/ Tier 1. Topics: 12. Why: explicit pros/cons lists including flicker, performance, secrecy, and omnichannel.

Google Optimize Alternatives in 2026. goprecision.co / mida.so. https://goprecision.co/blog/google-optimize-alternatives/ Tier 3. Topics: 12. Why: the September 30 2023 sunset date and the current free/paid tool split (Statsig free to 1M events, GrowthBook open source).

Towards Optimal Variance Reduction in Online Controlled Experiments (LinkedIn). Jin, Ba et al. arXiv 2110.13406, 2021. https://arxiv.org/pdf/2110.13406 Tier 2. Topics: 7. Why: the hard number showing CUPED's ceiling on volatile revenue metrics (15.91% variance reduction on n=400,000), the key evidence for why CUPED underdelivers on DTC revenue.

Considered and rejected

Generic "A/B testing statistics" listicles quoting round win-rate numbers with no sample (multiple). Rejected: violate the no-sample-size rule; win rates cited without the test count or confidence threshold.

Vendor case studies claiming large lifts (e.g. "+364%") without stating sample, duration, and baseline. Rejected under Twyman's law; these are the single most common source of bad knowledge in this field. Keep only as unvalidated hypothesis material.

abtestpro.com and similar auto-generated calculator/learn pages. Rejected as primary: they restate Evan Miller correctly but add no independent evidence; cite Miller directly instead.

HubSpot "20,000 rule" post. Partially used for the claim-2 check only; rejected as a general source because it is email-list-oriented and the round-number rule does not generalise across baselines.

LinkedIn and Medium opinion posts without data. Rejected as Tier 4 except where they present a named simulation (Molas) or concrete platform numbers (Atticus Li).

Notes on confidence and conflicts

The sample-size tables from calculator sites agree with each other and with Evan Miller's n=16 formula to within rounding. Treat them as reliable. Small differences between calculators come from the leading constant (Miller uses a value slightly below 16) and from pooled vs unpooled variance.

unit.title: Bayesian tests still mislead when stopped on peeking thresholds

claim.text: The source states Bayesian A/B testing is not immune to peeking, reporting a simulation with about an 80% false positive rate when peeking every 100 observations and stopping at P(A>B)>0.95.
claim.quote: simulation showing about 80% false positive rate when peeking every 100 obs and stopping at P(A>B)>0.95

args.text: Peeking every 100 observations and stopping when P(A>B)>0.95.
args.quote: peeking every 100 obs and stopping at P(A>B)>0.95
